LESSON: FRACTIONS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 1.7: Fractions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fractions, part of NUMBERS in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: How can you represent a half, a quarter or an eighth of a group?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign different types of fractions and terms related to fractions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fractions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify a 1 2 as part of a whole in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fractions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. identify a 1 4 as part of a whole in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fractions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. use fractions in day-to-day activities, appreciate the application of fractions in daily life activities. ● Learners in pairs or groups to be guided to identify, fingerspell and sign fractions, proper fraction, improper fraction, mixed fraction, numerator and denominator. ● In pairs, use papers, pencils and a pair of scissors to make circular paper cut-outs while observing safety. ● In pairs, fold the circular paper cut-outs into two equal parts and identify one of the parts as a half of the whole written as 1 2 . ● In pairs, make rectangular paper cut-outs and fold them into two equal parts to get a half of a whole written as 1 2 . ● In pairs, fold circular paper cut-outs to get 4 equal parts and identify one of the parts as a 1 4 of a whole. ● In pairs, practice making halves and quarters of a whole. ● Play games involving fractions using digital devices or other resources. How can you represent a half, a quarter or an eighth of a group? Core-Competencies to be developed: • Critical thinking and problem solving: Communication skill is developed as learners discuss in pairs or in groups how to divide a number of objects into 8 equal groups and identify each of the small groups as eighth of a whole.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fractions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. sign different types of fractions and terms related to fractions,

   Fractions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. identify a 1 2 as part of a whole in different situations,

   Fractions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. identify a 1 4 as part of a whole in different situations,

   Fractions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. use fractions in day-to-day activities, appreciate the application of fractions in daily life activities. ● Learners in pairs or groups to be guided to identify, fingerspell and sign fractions, proper fraction, improper fraction, mixed fraction, numerator and denominator. ● In pairs, use papers, pencils and a pair of scissors to make circular paper cut-outs while observing safety. ● In pairs, fold the circular paper cut-outs into two equal parts and identify one of the parts as a half of the whole written as 1 2 . ● In pairs, make rectangular paper cut-outs and fold them into two equal parts to get a half of a whole written as 1 2 . ● In pairs, fold circular paper cut-outs to get 4 equal parts and identify one of the parts as a 1 4 of a whole. ● In pairs, practice making halves and quarters of a whole. ● Play games involving fractions using digital devices or other resources. How can you represent a half, a quarter or an eighth of a group? Core-Competencies to be developed: • Critical thinking and problem solving: Communication skill is developed as learners discuss in pairs or in groups how to divide a number of objects into 8 equal groups and identify each of the small groups as eighth of a whole.

   Fractions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fractions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Unity: The spirit of cooperation is enhanced as learners work as a team to make rectangular cut-outs and fold them into 4 equal parts

to get a quarter of a whole.

14

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: Learners in pairs or in groups to safely make circular cut-outs from manila papers.

Link to other learning areas:

• Learners are guided to make rectangular cut-outs and fold to get 8 equal parts and identify one part as 1⁄8 of the whole.

Suggested Learning resources:

● Circular and rectangular cut outs, marbles, bottle tops, sticks, grains, stones, manilla papers
